newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Pinochet leaves hospital after fainting spell.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Pinochet leaves hospital after fainting spell.

text.p: Former Chilean dictator Gen. Augusto Pinochet left a military hospital on Sunday in the city of Arica where he spent a day after fainting at a dinner.

His doctor said he would continue to monitor the 82-year-old general, who heads the Chilean army, before deciding if he can fly back to Santiago. Arica is a coastal city located in the far north on the border with Peru.
Pinochet fainted during a dinner celebrating the 117th anniversary of the battle of El Morro, a major episode in Chile's war against Peru and Bolivia.
His doctor Jaime Gonzalez said on Saturday he had suffered a drop in his blood pressure associated with gastrointestinal problems.
He said Pinochet slept well and his vital signs were stable, but said he should remain under observation for a while before travelling again.
Pinochet was scheduled to end his tenure as head of the army in March 1998, after 25 years in the job.
The general took power in Chile in a bloody 1973 coup and ruled the country until 1990, when democracy was re-established. His brutal military regime was charged with numerous human rights abuses.
In a pre-taped interview broadcast on Saturday night on Chilean television, Pinochet was asked how he remained in such good health. He said he exercised every day.
